study: Line heads in the four-family model
kind: pre-registration: two trainings on the laptop's GPU and twelve practice runs on the server's GPU in the window Daniel opened until Thursday 2026-12-03 07:45 Berlin
why: line_heads_in_practice.json passed both of its readings: with two of every read's four heads counting lines, three practised stacks write 0.880, 0.770 and 0.815 of 20-step chains whole, their controls 0.080, 0.000 and 0.070, and all six runs hold. Its registered consequence is this record: the four-family corpus is trained again with line heads, and practice_several_families.json's questions are asked with that model, with --dips 0 because practice_that_stands.json did not pass. Two-family practice from four-stack is where the loop has fallen: five of six --dips 0 runs broke past the corpus's lengths (practice_several_families.json, practice_that_stands.json), and the dip kept four of six standing.

arms.four-line-stack: four-stack's recipe (written_chains_four_families.json, checkpoints/laptop-loop/run-four.sh: the delayed test bed of width 256 and depth 6 on data/onemodel/chains/four-1-4-written.bin, 24,000 updates, seed 20001, peak rate 1.2e-3, streams of 10 windows of 256 bytes) with --read-word-heads 2 --read-word-unit line --read-word-span 256 (line_heads.json's line heads) and --read-by-cell, on the laptop's GPU with the frozen code copy code-833ff4d; 5,252,132 parameters.
arms.four-cell-stack: four-stack's recipe with --read-by-cell, the same code and device: the control, trained after it on the laptop. Line heads have no read by age, so both take every read by cell (the same spikes, tests/test_word_heads.py); four-stack itself trained on other code and is not the control. 5,249,060 parameters.
arms.practice: From each base, practice_several_families.json's arm 'all': the families the base learned, practised in the same rounds, with that record's loop and --dips 0: --families hops offs --longest-hops 12 --dips 0 --rehearse 16 --evaluate-hops 2 4 8 12 --exact-products --seed N for seeds 0 to 5, so line-all-s0 to -s5 and cell-all-s0 to -s5. The families are hops and offs if both bases learned them by written_chains_four_families.json's rule (a mean accuracy over 1 to 4 steps of at least 0.95 and a mean share of whole chains of at least 0.90); a family that only one base learned is practised by neither, and the record says so before any practice run starts. Neither arm takes --fused-reads, which line heads do not have. Code copy v18s (833ff4d) on the server, as experiments/practice_loop.py was smoke-tested on the laptop on 2026-11-28.

measure.the bases: After training, on the server: experiments/practice_loop.py --families hops offs sums tots --evaluate 1 2 3 4 5 6 8 12 16 --evaluate-tasks 200 --max-bytes 64 --seed 0 on both averaged weights (accuracy with its 95% Wilson interval, whole chains, mean bytes), and the probe of recall_over_distance.json; the trainer's validation on streams after 24,000 updates.
measure.the practice runs: practice_several_families.json's measure and marks: along the way, before the first round and every 100 rounds, 200 tasks of 2, 4, 8 and 12 steps a family; after the last round --evaluate 1 2 3 4 5 6 8 12 16 --evaluate-tasks 200 --max-bytes 64 --seed 0 for every family; kept, held, reach and reach kept, and a run holds if every practised family meets all four. The answers of every run that does not hold are counted by form (experiments/forms_families.py on the server's CPU).

reading.(1) line heads keep the two-family loop: If all six line-all runs hold. If any falls, its rounds are read before anything is built on it.
reading.(2) line heads practise further: For each practised family, the share of whole chains at 12 and at 16 steps after practice, line-all against cell-all seed by seed (the same seed in both arms). Line heads practise further in a family if line-all is ahead (at least 0.10 higher with the two 95% intervals apart) at either length in at least four of the six seeds and behind at neither length in any seed; cell-all practises further by the same rule the other way; otherwise neither. Read for each family.
reading.(3) the control's loop: How many cell-all runs hold, beside the one of six --dips 0 runs from four-stack that held: reported.
reading.reported and not read: The bases' cells by family and step count, their probes and validations, every cell after practice, the evaluations along the way, the staircases, and how any run that does not hold writes.
reading.scope: Two families of synthetic chains, one training of each base, six seeds of practice: whether line heads keep practice on several families standing, not a claim about reasoning in language.

what follows: If (1) holds and (2) finds line heads ahead in both families, the one-model stack takes line heads: the next practice registrations (more families, replay past the rehearsed lengths) start from four-line-stack. If (1) holds and (2) does not, line heads hold the loop up but do not lengthen two-family practice, and replay is tried from four-line-stack. If (1) fails, the fallen runs are read first, and replay (practice_loop.py --replay) is the next candidate.
where: The two trainings on the laptop's GPU one after the other, about two hours each, from 2026-11-28 ~10:00 UTC; their averaged weights copied to the server's tmp/practice/models/. The base evaluations and probes on the server's CPU. The twelve practice runs as two GPU jobs of six (three seeds of each arm in a job, so that both arms share every job's conditions), after the full-size runs queued ahead of them; at most one model's arms share a GPU, as the practice runner requires.
seen_before_recording: line_heads.json's and line_heads_in_practice.json's results, practice_several_families.json's and practice_that_stands.json's results (both halves), and a 40-round smoke run of --replay from four-stack on the laptop. No four-family model with line heads exists.
